[spoiler=[u][b]*Claim[/b][/u]]The years following the 77-Day War saw a fundamental change in the fate of the Oceanice Republic. Having established itself militarily, the Republic looked inward to drive the development of its economy and outward to provide it with new resources and markets, sparking what would eventually be known as the Great Industrial Era of West Argos. By the early 1880s, Oceanice merchants and tycoons flooded trade routes across the seas, sending their vessels full of coal, steel goods, textiles, and machinery into foreign harbors, returning with silks, spices, and above all the prized minerals that would shape the century to come: uranium and plutonium. Kyoukai, a proud empire governed by the Relkan species, a feline-descended furry people whose civilization had thrived on the southern island chains for centuries, became a partner and rival during this era of restless expansion. The Kyoukai clans possessed abundant deposits of ore, tea, sugar, and fine commodities, and Oceanice's early industrial giants negotiated with their leaders, trading weapons, refined goods, and industrial machinery for raw wealth.
But this relationship, like so many throughout Oceanice's history, was poisoned by mistrust and ideology. The ascendance of Humanism and the increasingly firm hold of fascist ideology in the Republic rendered trade with furry civilizations perilous and disdainful. Trade continued, but Kyoukai rulers increasingly regarded Oceanice merchants as dangerous necessities. Emperor Shujia Kal, who ascended to the throne in the early 1910s, personified this distrust. A cunning orator and tactician, he had observed with growing alarm the Oceanice push into West Argos and the violence with which its regime oppressed native furry populations. In the eyes of Shujia Kal, every Oceanice merchant was a spy, not merely a trader, and every rifle exported a potential fetter on Kyoukai sovereignty. By December of 1913, following repeated altercations in port cities, allegations of espionage, and pressure from Relkan nobles, Emperor Shujia Kal announced the severance of all commercial relations with Oceanice. On the 3rd of that month, his court declared Oceanice citizens enemies of the state. Ships were prohibited, warehouses confiscated, and the Oceanice community throughout the Kyoukai archipelago expelled or jailed.
Bismarck the Great, chancellor of Oceanice and architect of its modern military, was confronted with an outcry at home. His councilors called for war at once, demanding revenge for the affront to the Republic's honor and the danger to its burgeoning commercial empire. But Bismarck, tempered by the experience of the 77-Day War, was wary. He did not wish another drawn-out conflict that could destabilize Oceanice industry just as it was approaching new peaks. Instead, he dispatched a delegation in the hope of preserving peace: two human diplomats, attired in ceremonial black, and one furry translator, himself a Relkan who had dwelled in Berlienwerk for decades. They braved the stormy straits to the Kyoukai capital, their task uncomplicated  to negotiate a resumption of trade on new terms, offering the Empire assurances of sovereignty while providing Oceanice access to the vital uranium and rare goods it so desperately needed.
But the mission ended in blood. Shujia Kal, believing the translator was a traitor to his own kind and infuriated by what he perceived as arrogance in the human envoys, had them arrested at court. The two human representatives were tossed into jail without trial, while the translator was hauled to the palace steps and beheaded publicly for treason. Word of this execution arrived at Berlienwerk within days, brought by panicked surviving sailors and merchants who had been expelled from Kyoukai. Bismarck the Great, usually a man of restraint, went into what one general later described as "a wrath fit to darken the sky itself." He pounded his fist upon the war table, declaring that no Relkan insult would be unanswered, no furry empire would be permitted to spit upon the Republic and live. Plans began immediately for an invasion of the southern islands.
January 3rd, 1914 was the starting day of what history would call the Kyoukai War. At sunrise, the Oceanice Navy set sail from its ports in West Argos, fleets of dreadnoughts and cruisers carrying the tricolor flag across the winter seas. They were not medieval warships or colonial frigates, but rather modern ships of steel hammered in the forges of the Great Industrial Era, mounting heavy-caliber naval rifles copied from the world's great powers of the Great War. In their wake came troop transports carrying infantrymen in gray coats, helmets shining under the pale winter sun, bayonets fixed, and artillery batteries tied down with chains. At their forefront was Bismarck himself, old but unbowed, commanding the invasion with a genius for logistics that had made him both feared and respected by his contemporaries. His plan was simple but merciless: attack the southernmost island of the archipelago first, take its harbors, secure a beachhead, and then march northwards until the Kyoukai Empire knelt.
The defenders of Relkan were not unprepared. Shujia Kal, forewarned of Oceanice aggression, had mobilized his warriors  proud feline troops who bore rifles of older model, many bought from Lavian or captured in previous wars, along with ancient swords and spears still used by the clans. Kyoukai forts dotted the southern coastlines, their stone walls supported by cannon reclaimed from previous centuries. But against the steel wave of Oceanice industry, they would be stretched to the breaking point. The first battle occurred on January 7th, when Oceanice dreadnoughts opened fire on Fort Naikara, the great fortress guarding the southern island of Yutsen. Shells shrieked across the heavens before crashing into the fortress walls, sending stone and bodies flying. Relkan gunners responded in kind, but their salvoes bounced off the armored hulls of Oceanice battleships, while return barrages shattered the fort to rubble.
When the Oceanice infantry landed on the beaches that same morning, they were greeted by a hail of bullets and arrows from Relkan defenders who fought with desperate courage. Waves of Relkan troops poured from the woods, their feline shapes swift and lithe, curved sabers flashing in close combat. For a moment, the gray-coated invaders wavered, flailing in the mud as bayonets clashed with blades. But discipline and firepower won the day. Machine gun nests were hauled ashore, vomiting death into charging ranks, while artillery was wheeled into place to blast pockets of resistance flat. By dusk, the beaches ran red with blood, and the Oceanice flag flew over the smoking wreckage of Fort Naikara. The southern island was theirs.
For six months the war convulsed the archipelago. Every island was its own battleground, a savage meeting of industrial war and ancient custom. In Yutsen's jungles, Relkan warriors waged a guerrilla war, ambushing supply lines and dissolving back into the trees. Oceanice troops, unaccustomed to the landscape, lost heavily in the opening months, their gray fatigues poorly suited to the close, wet forests. Disease and fatigue took almost as many lives as Relkan swords. But Oceanice learned with ruthless effectiveness. Flamethrowers and poison gas, technologies imported from the broader Great War raging on the continents, were brought into the fight. Villages thought to be sheltering guerrillas were incinerated, their populations shot or pushed into camps. Whole swaths of jungle were burned to prevent cover for the Relkan soldiers.
By March, the war had reached the center of the Kyoukai Empire. Oceanice troops moved north, their navy shelling coastal cities as soldiers marched inland, taking farmland and railroads. Shujia Kal, not willing to give up, rallied his people in the capital city, a majestic city of stone temples and wood palaces on a high hill. Here the Relkans made their final stand, barricading the streets and summoning every citizen capable of bearing arms. For weeks, the city was under siege, its walls day and night pounded by Oceanice artillery. Food became scarce, water was rationed, and still the Relkans fought, sniping from rooftops, setting traps in alleys, charging with rifle and sword in hand against tanks rolling through their gates.
On the 18th of June, 1914, the capital fell. Oceanice forces stormed the palace, killing guards and pulling Shujia Kal from his throne. The proud emperor, refusing to kneel, spat curses at his captors before being shot in front of his own people. With his death, the Kyoukai Empire dissolved. Resistance raged in the jungles and mountains for weeks, but the heart of the nation had been lost. Bismarck proclaimed victory, raising the Oceanice flag over the burning ruins of the capital, announcing the archipelago annexed into the Republic. The Kyoukai islands, once an independent empire of the Relkan people, were reduced to provinces ruled over by Oceanice administrators, their resources taken, their culture suppressed, their people sent to labor camps or assimilation programs intended to erase their heritage.
And so concluded the Kyoukai War, the six-month campaign that showcased both the strength and the brutality of the Oceanice Republic. The conflict between human supremacist ambition and the sovereignty of a proud furry civilization. For Oceanice, it was a victory, winning uranium and plutonium reserves that would power its ascension to nuclear power in the decades that followed. For the Relkans, it was a tragedy, the end of their empire and the start of decades of occupation, resistance, and erasure. It was a watershed in incorporating the whole Empire as a part of Oceanice Republic

Following the capitulation of the Kyoukai Empire in the summer of 1914, the Oceanice Republic did not content itself with imposing simple terms of surrender; it acted with calculated vengeance to eliminate the last remnants of the old regime that had once presumed to challenge its power. Annexation of the island was rapid, but the consequences were imbued with an unmistakable atmosphere of revenge. Republic soldiers poured into the capital city of the Relkan furries, a city that had endured for centuries as the center of the Kyoukai dynasty, its great pagodas and ancestral halls shining in the morning sun. At the city's center lay the great imperial palace, a huge complex of wood, lacquered stone, and intricate carvings portraying the history and glory of the Relkan rulers. To the conquerors, however, it represented defiance a reminder of the insults and humiliation which had precipitated war.
What ensued was not an orderly occupation but a deliberate show of dominance. The palace was denuded of its riches first Oceanice troops, as well as opportunistic traders and even some human settlers who had trailed the army, plundering the halls, ripping tapestries from walls, wrenching gold from shrines, and breaking open ceremonial armor and crowns. Irreplaceable artifacts of the Kyoukai emperors, some of which dated back to the founding of their dynasty, were taken away as spoils to Berlienwerk. Even the imperial archives, containing centuries of history and genealogies, were hauled away, leaving the cultural memory of the Relkan people in shreds.

Looting soon made way for fire. Torches were hurled into the once-splendid halls, lacquered wood igniting with a roar and hiss, faster than the city's defenders could respond. By night, the palace was ablaze in fire visible for miles, a towering pyre that sent the sky red and black. Soldiers sang songs of triumph as the great roofs caved inward, their shouts drowning out the roar of burning history. Witnesses told of statues of ancient kings melting into shapeless blobs of bronze, and sacred gardens, once hallowed places of meditation, burned to ash. The devastation was so complete that by dawn, there was little left of the palace but smoldering rubble and a few half-intact walls.[/spoiler]

- The Neue Republik will withdraw all military forces from Hydronian land and territorial waters
- The commonwealth of Karcovshkie will withdraw all military forces from Hydronian land and territorial waters
- THEP and its member states will end all sanctions on the Neue Republik
- Subsidiaries of Republik companies will access the Hydronian market under Hydronian regulations to help rebuild civilian infrastructure designated to them by the Hydronian Federal government
- The Neue Republik will be granted council of 6 status in the IA
[/list]

Additionally, a ceasefire will be enforced for the time it takes for the withdrawal of troops.
